# Plan Quality Checklist: Eino Supervisor Template

**Purpose**: Review whether the merged execution plan states complete, clear, consistent, and measurable requirements for observability, synthetic operations, MySQL, approval, and recovery.
**Created**: 2026-09-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) and [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Does the merged plan explicitly distinguish completed M0-M8 capability, remaining M9-M12 work, and deferred C039/C042 evidence rather than mixing implementation status with future requirements? [Completeness, Spec §Runtime Extension Requirements]
- [x] CHK002 Are the three user stories each mapped to a complete goal, independent test, acceptance scenarios, and remaining implementation scope? [Completeness, Spec §User Scenarios & Testing]
- [x] CHK003 Does the plan define the full observability field set across logs, traces, metrics, files, OTLP/Langfuse export, and degradation behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023–FR-031]
- [x] CHK004 Does the MySQL scope define schema, Tool inputs/outputs, approval, idempotency, error classes, tracing, and optional Compose dependencies without requiring a new HTTP endpoint? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019–FR-021; contracts/mysql-gorm.md]
- [x] CHK005 Are default zero-credential behavior and optional external dependencies clearly separated from local contract requirements? [Completeness, Plan §Technical Context; Spec §Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Are terms such as “完整可观测性”, “安全摘要”, “低基数”, “有限步骤”, and “可恢复” defined with concrete fields, limits, or allowed values? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023–FR-029]
- [x] CHK007 Is the exact boundary between an observation failure, a business failure, and `RUN_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` stated consistently in the spec, contracts, and plan? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, FR-026–FR-027; contracts/runtime-foundation.md]
- [x] CHK008 Are the allowed W3C propagation behaviors for missing, malformed, and valid `traceparent`/`tracestate` unambiguous? [Clarity, contracts/http-sse.md; contracts/observability.md]
- [x] CHK009 Are MySQL decimal precision, quantity positivity, foreign-key requirements, payload size, and unknown-field rejection stated in one authoritative place without conflicting limits? [Clarity, data-model.md; contracts/mysql-gorm.md]
- [x] CHK010 Does the plan state exactly when an approved side-effect operation may acquire a database transaction and how the application-derived idempotency key is formed? [Clarity, contracts/mysql-gorm.md]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 Are the “single Worker before multi Worker/database” ordering rule and the “observability before MySQL” rule consistent across `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and `quickstart.md`? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018/F​R-022; Plan §Phases]
- [x] CHK012 Do the plan and tasks consistently treat `docs/scaffold-evolution-plan.md` as background constraints rather than a second executable plan? [Consistency, Plan §Summary; docs/architecture.md]
- [x] CHK013 Are approval, Policy Gate, idempotency, checkpoint, and terminal-state ownership assigned to the same Application/Manager boundary in every contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004–FR-007; contracts/http-sse.md; contracts/runtime-foundation.md]
- [x] CHK014 Are the claims about “same trace_id across resume” reconciled with the distinction between a new HTTP request span and the persisted run correlation identifier? [Conflict, contracts/observability.md; tasks.md T033]
- [x] CHK015 Do the stated limits for two-step serial execution, no parallel/DAG behavior, and no Worker-created steps agree across scope, acceptance criteria, and deferred work? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016/FR-018; Plan §Technical Context]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK016 Can each observability success criterion be objectively judged from named fields, span names, labels, headers, file permissions, or degradation signals rather than the word “完整”? [Measurability, Spec §SC-011–SC-015]
- [x] CHK017 Are the 5-second P1 target, repeated-approval count, retry prohibition, and single-terminal-event requirements tied to explicit test conditions and scope? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-006]
- [x] CHK018 Are MySQL acceptance criteria explicit about both successful query/insert evidence and failure evidence for validation, foreign keys, unavailable database, timeout, and unknown commit? [Measurability, contracts/mysql-gorm.md]
- [x] CHK019 Does each remaining task have a corresponding requirement or contract reference so a reviewer can determine why the task exists and when it is complete? [Traceability, tasks.md]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [x] CHK020 Are primary, alternate, rejection, cancellation, client-disconnect, exporter-outage, and resume scenarios all specified for the existing `/api/chat` flow? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios & Testing; contracts/http-sse.md]
- [x] CHK021 Are partial-failure boundaries explicit for pre-call failure, in-flight cancellation, commit ambiguity, projection failure, and missing event replay? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases; contracts/runtime-foundation.md]
- [x] CHK022 Are duplicate approval, duplicate resume, duplicate cancel, duplicate event IDs, and repeated approved inserts covered as requirements rather than only as implementation tasks? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005/FR-006; contracts/http-sse.md]
- [x] CHK023 Are malformed model decisions, unknown Worker/Tool references, oversized or extra-field payloads, and unsupported natural-language query criteria intentionally fail-closed? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008; data-model.md]
- [x] CHK024 Are missing or invalid observation configuration, unavailable Langfuse/Collector, unwritable files, and rotation/retention boundary behavior specified? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-027–FR-031; contracts/observability.md]

## Non-Functional and Security Requirements

- [x] CHK025 Are all sensitive-data exclusions consistent across logs, traces, metrics, SSE, files, OTLP/Langfuse, database errors, and Tool outputs? [Security, Spec §FR-023/FR-026/FR-030; contracts/observability.md]
- [x] CHK026 Are authentication/resource ownership and model-action Policy Gate explicitly kept separate for the new MySQL and observability paths? [Security, Spec §FR-011–FR-012]
- [x] CHK027 Are performance and resource ceilings defined for steps, Tool calls, model loops, deadlines, costs, payloads, output sizes, log rotation, and retention? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003/FR-014/FR-015; Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK028 Does the requirements set explicitly exclude production HA, multi-instance observation aggregation, cross-process exactly-once, forced process termination, and real customer/CRM writes? [Scope, Spec §FR-028; Plan §Constraints; Spec §Assumptions]

## Dependencies, Assumptions, and Ambiguities

- [x] CHK029 Are the required Go/library versions and optional GORM/MySQL/OTel components aligned with the repository's actual dependency policy and described as implementation choices rather than user-visible guarantees? [Dependency, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK030 Are the assumptions behind local fake data, static Bearer authentication, single-instance files, and optional Docker/Collector explicit enough to prevent accidental production interpretation? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions; PROGRESS.md]
- [x] CHK031 Is the source of truth for current status unambiguous among `PROGRESS.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and the historical evolution document? [Clarity, Plan §Summary; docs/architecture.md]
- [x] CHK032 Are unresolved questions about cross-request trace continuity, exact observability retention defaults, and MySQL integration gating called out as `[Ambiguity]` items before implementation begins? [Ambiguity, Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after a reviewer confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when clarification, wording changes, or cross-document reconciliation is still needed.
- This checklist validates requirements writing; it does not certify implementation or runtime behavior.
- `$speckit-implement` may read checklist state as a gate but must not modify these markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` remains the built-in spec-quality checklist maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
